normalization: Paired left/right bones count once per named concept.
Auditory/acoustic and body/centrum synonyms count once.
Zygomatic process and entire zygomatic arch are separate concepts.
Sternal and acromial clavicular ends are separate concepts.
Medial and lateral femoral condyles are separate concepts.
Repeated names on different parent bones remain separate.
Manubrium and xiphoid process are tracked separately from the complete sternum.
pageConvention: All source.pages are 1-based pages in the 61-page uploaded Top Hat export, not print textbook page numbers.
figureNumbering: Some export captions conflict with nearby prose (lateral skull, scapula, forearm, pelvis). Those entries use page references and a null figure instead of inventing a corrected caption number.

corrections.issue: The lab claims a direct ulnar-head/lunate articulation and describes carpals as articulating with both radius and ulna.
corrections.used: The distal ulna is separated from the carpals by fibrocartilaginous structures; its head articulates with the distal radius.

corrections.issue: The lab claims all thoracic vertebral foramina are approximately triangular.
corrections.used: The card uses rib articulation and typical spinous-process shape; it does not teach a universal triangle rule. Typical thoracic foramina are generally circular.

corrections.used: Added anterior knee location, triangular shape, leverage function, and a qualified larger-lateral-facet side cue.

geometry: This dataset establishes vocabulary and study-card content only. It does not assert 3D mesh availability, exact landmark segmentation, label coordinates, or quiz coverage.
implementationNotes: Hyoid is grouped under Skull for the requested fixed region enumeration, but its location field correctly states superior neck. Consider labeling that navigation region Skull & neck.
Cervical, thoracic, and lumbar vertebrae are bone-family concepts; atlas and axis are separate required concepts.
Jugular foramen, sutures, zygomatic arch, and bilateral pelvic joints are associated with multiple bones rather than incorrectly assigned to one parent.
Generic vertebral spinous process, transverse process, lamina, and body have null parentId to avoid adding an unapproved generic vertebra entry.
Keep exact parent qualifiers for all repeated names when grading typed answers.
